claims.text: As-fabricated additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components may contain fabrication-induced defects.
Temperature, pressure, and scanning speed are process parameters that should be optimized for additive manufacturing of high-entropy alloys.
Process-parameter optimization will alter the microstructure of additively manufactured high-entropy alloys.
Optimized process parameters will reduce fabrication-induced defects.
Optimized process parameters will improve material properties.
Process-parameter optimization will improve dimensional precision.
Process-parameter optimization will improve mechanical integrity.
Dimensional precision and mechanical integrity will improve by 15% relative to the current fabrication baseline.
The proposed improvement should hold under the operating conditions in which the components are used.
The exact relationship between process parameters and material properties is not fully understood.
The hypothesis can be tested by a controlled experiment that varies process parameters and measures dimensional precision, mechanical integrity, and defect density.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% improvement in both dimensional precision and mechanical integrity would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvement is 15%, but the falsification threshold is only 10%. Results between 10% and 15% would fail to achieve the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
